title: A Garden for the Crown Again
premise: Isandro Dunmore, a bone-carver who hears the dead through the ivory he carves, keeps the ledgers of the Vellum Guild, which trades in impossible things — including debts owed by a country that was erased from every map forty years ago. When a dying courier presses a map of that vanished country into Isandro's hands, they inherit not just the map but the courier's unfinished bargain: find the door out before the debt comes due, or be collected along with everything else the Crown stole. Hunted by guild enforcers and guided by the increasingly urgent voices of the dead, Isandro discovers the 'door' is a person — the last living heir of the erased nation, hidden in plain sight as a guild clerk. In the end, Isandro must choose between paying the debt with the heir's life and carving their own bones into the ledger, erasing themselves so the heir and the vanished country's memory can walk free.
about_author: Yara Ishikawa is a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing estate sales before turning to fiction, a career she credits for her obsession with ledgers, inheritance, and what paperwork can bury. She writes in a converted greenhouse in Porto, where she claims the tomatoes listen better than most editors.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Ivory
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. A night in the Vellum Guild's counting house establishes Isandro's gift: the bone they carve speaks with the voices of its dead owners, and the ledgers record trades no sane market should allow. When a bloodied stranger collapses at the door clutching an oilskin packet, Isandro's instinct is to refuse him. The man dies pressing the packet into their hands anyway. Beat: reluctant witness.

chapters.title: A Map of Nowhere
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. The packet contains a map of Callowmere, a country struck from every record four decades ago, annotated in a dead woman's hand with a single instruction: the door opens at the debt's due date. Guild Master Corvane summons Isandro to ask what the courier carried; lying to Corvane is a survival skill Isandro has practiced all their life. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Bones Remember
chapters.summary: POV Isandro, interludes from the dead courier Sef's voice. Carving a memorial piece from Sef's recovered finger-bone, Isandro hears his last days: he was Callowmere's heir-apparent's sworn messenger, and the 'door out' is a living person, not a place. The dead give one clue — a guild clerk named Merrin Vale who signs her ledgers in a hand too old for her age. Beat: grief becoming purpose.

chapters.title: The Clerk with Two Handwritings
chapters.summary: POV alternating Isandro and Merrin. Isandro engineers a meeting with Merrin under pretense of ledger audit; Merrin, sharp and suspicious, recognizes the map's calligraphy as her grandmother's. She denies everything too quickly. Meanwhile Corvane sets enforcers on the courier's trail. Beat: wary alliance forming over shared denial.

chapters.title: Debt Collectors
chapters.summary: POV Merrin. Guild enforcers ransack Merrin's rooms seeking the map; she escapes through the archive stacks using routes only clerks know, meeting Isandro in the bone-vault below. There, shelves of carved remains whisper the truth Corvane has buried: the Guild financed Callowmere's erasure and has been collecting interest on it ever since. Beat: horror at complicity.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Fugitives now, they follow the map into the salt marshes where Callowmere's border once stood. Isandro confesses their own history: as a child they survived the purge by carving false records for the Guild, trading silence for bread. Merrin must decide whether an accomplice can be trusted with her country's last hope. Beat: confession and fragile forgiveness.

chapters.title: Where the Country Went
chapters.summary: POV both, converging. At the drowned border-stone, the dead of Callowmere rise through the marsh water — not as monsters but as witnesses, showing them the night of the erasure and revealing the door's mechanism: it opens only if someone willingly enters the ledger as payment. Corvane's enforcers close in across the flats. Beat: awe curdling to dread.

chapters.title: Corvane's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Captured and brought before Corvane, Isandro learns the full ledger: the Guild owes Callowmere a debt it can never pay honestly, so Corvane intends to pay it dishonestly — with Merrin's life, closing the account forever and freeing the Guild of guilt. He offers Isandro their old bargain again: silence for survival. Beat: temptation at its strongest.

chapters.title: The Door Opens Inward
chapters.summary: POV Merrin, climax. On the due date, at the ruined capital, Corvane forces the ritual; but Isandro, having secretly carved their own name into the master ledger, steps through the door in Merrin's place. The dead accept the payment of a willing debtor. Merrin, screaming, crosses the threshold as it seals — and finds herself not dead but standing in a Callowmere that exists only in memory, holding the map. Beat: sacrifice and reversal.

chapters.title: A Garden for the Crown Again
chapters.summary: POV Merrin, coda. Merrin returns alone to a country that still refuses to remember hers, carrying Sef's bones and Isandro's last carving — a small gate, through which, on quiet nights, a voice still speaks. She plants a garden on the drowned border-stone and begins writing a new ledger in two hands: what was taken, and what was given back. Beat: mourning transmuted into testimony.
